# Region Nordjylland

Region Nordjylland is one of the five administrative regions of Denmark participating in the [[dansk-kvalitetsdatabase-for-inflammatoriske-tarmsygdomme|Dansk Kvalitetsdatabase for Inflammatoriske Tarmsygdomme]] (DANIBD), alongside [[region-hovedstaden|Region Hovedstaden]], [[region-sjaelland|Region Sjælland]], [[region-syddanmark|Region Syddanmark]], and [[region-midtjylland|Region Midtjylland]]. As a key stakeholder in the national effort to systematize and improve the treatment of inflammatory bowel disease (IBD), the region contributes patient data and provides members to the DANIBD steering group, illustrating the regional implementation of the national registry [^src1].

In the reporting period from October 1, 2022, to September 30, 2023, Region Nordjylland registered a total of 3,572 IBD patients [^src1]. The diagnostic distribution within the region showed that [[dk50-crohns-sygdom|DK50* Crohns sygdom]] accounted for 40% of all IBD patients, while [[dk51-ulceroes-colitis|DK51* Ulcerøs colitis]] made up 60% [^src1]. Additionally, the region recorded 14 patients with [[dk830f-primaer-skleroserende-kolangitis|DK830F Primær skleroserende kolangitis]] [^src1].

Despite its active participation, the region has faced challenges in meeting specific quality indicators. In the [[danibd-aarsrapport-2024]] it was noted that Region Nordjylland was far from the target for [[indikator-1b|Indikator 1b]] (complete diagnostic workup for children and youth on time), achieving only a 38% fulfillment rate [^src3]. 

In response to the 2024 annual report, Region Nordjylland submitted formal feedback outlining operational improvements. For [[indikator-2|Indikator 2]], which tracks patient education, the region plans to increase its focus on correct registration practices for newly diagnosed patients receiving education within a year of diagnosis, utilizing the [[bike1-undervisning-i-inflammatorisk-tarmsygdom|BIKE1 - Undervisning i inflammatorisk tarmsygdom]] SKS code [^src5]. Furthermore, to improve performance on Indicator 4 regarding [[dexa-scanning|DEXA-scanning]] for IBD patients over 50 receiving steroid treatments, the region intends to modify workflows to allow nurses and secretaries in the Department of Gastroenterology to order DEXA scans directly, and will attempt to retroactively register and order scans for patients to be included in the 2025 annual report [^src5].
